questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), calculate the difference between India’s share of world exports of rice in 2010 and 2022. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Which one of the following would not be classified by an economist as a factor of production?
options: Labour temporarily out of work
Money in a firm’s bank account
Non-agricultural land
Risk-taking entrepreneurs

questions.questionText: Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 1 and Figure 2) show that the rice export ban by India in 2022 is likely to have had a significant impact on the world price of rice.

The central purpose of economic activity is the production of goods and services to satisfy needs and wants. Which of the following is one of the three key decisions that has to be taken to achieve this?
options: How to achieve economies of scale
What goods and services to produce
Where to locate businesses
Whether to maximise profit or sales

questions.questionText: Extract B (line 19) states: ‘In Nigeria, the demand for rice is very price inelastic’. With the help of a diagram, explain how the Indian export ban is likely to have affected the market for rice in Nigeria.
Figure 1 shows the market demand for electric cars. The shift of the market demand curve from D1 to D2 would most likely be caused by
options: a fall in the price of electric cars.
a government subsidy to producers of electric cars.
a marketing campaign promoting electric cars.
a reduction in the price of petrol and diesel fuels.

questions.questionText: Extract C (lines 6–7) states: ‘An alternative would be to impose a maximum price for consumers, as both Sri Lanka and the Philippines have done’. Using the data and your knowledge of economics, evaluate the view that imposing a maximum price for rice is the best way for a rice-importing nation, such as Nigeria, to ensure the affordability of a basic food for its citizens.
A firm hopes to increase its market share by setting its prices lower than most of its competitors. What is the most likely reason for this strategy?
options: The firm has a licence that gives it a temporary monopoly
The firm is a price taker in a very competitive market
The firm is aiming to differentiate its products from its competitors
The firm is aiming to increase its long-run profits

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the median number of storm overflow hours by water company in 2022.

A firm allows customers to personalise a mug with a name of their choice, which it sells for £15. The firm pays £3 for each mug. The paint and labour cost an extra £7. The firm has fixed costs of £150 per month and in a typical month, it produces and sells 60 mugs. What is the average cost of producing one personalised mug?
Explain how the data in Extract D (Figure 4) show that household water bills have increased in real terms since privatisation in 1989.
One reason why merit goods, such as education and health care, can lead to market failure is that
options: individuals are unwilling to pay for merit goods.
individuals have incomplete information about merit goods.
merit goods are generally provided free by the government.
merit goods are subject to the free-rider problem.

questions.questionText: Extract E (line 10) states: ‘The minimum efficient scale in the water industry is large’. With the help of a diagram, explain why the large minimum efficient scale in the water industry is likely to lead to the market being supplied by a few large firms with monopoly power.
Figure 2 shows the market for a good. S1 shows the supply if only private costs are considered and S2 shows the supply if social costs are taken into account. At the free market output, there is
options: a negative externality and overproduction of the good.
a negative externality and underproduction of the good.
a positive externality and overproduction of the good.
a positive externality and underproduction of the good.

questions.questionText: Extract F (lines 5–6) states: ‘if regulators impose fines, these costs may be passed on to consumers or reduce investment’. Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that stronger regulation would be a better policy than bringing the water industry back into public ownership.

Microchips are used in a wide range of products, including mobile phones and traffic lights. If demand increases for one of these products, this affects the price of other products that need microchips. This is an example of
options: complementary goods.
composite demand.
joint supply.
substitute goods.

questions.questionText: Explain, with examples, the differences between a private good, a public good and a quasi-public good.
A firm uses a variety of strategies to improve its market position. Which one of the following strategies is most likely to benefit consumers in the long run?
options: An advertising campaign that promotes the product’s image
Charging low prices to drive rival firms out of the market
Investing in research and development to improve product quality
Merging with a rival to reduce competition in the market

questions.questionText: Evaluate the view that oligopolies serve society well.
Table 1 shows the percentage market share of firms in a particular industry in 2020 and 2023. What was the change in the three-firm concentration ratio over the period 2020 to 2023?
options: A fall of 6 percentage points
A fall of 7 percentage points
A rise of 4 percentage points
A rise of 5 percentage points

questions.questionText: Explain how technological progress can affect productivity, efficiency and firms’ costs of production.
All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to result in a fall in the market price of rice?
options: Farmers releasing less rice for sale
Good weather conditions for growing rice
More wheat being planted instead of rice
The removal of a subsidy for growing rice

questions.questionText: Assess the view that the main objective of firms is to maximise profits.
Which one of the following is most likely to influence the price elasticity of supply of a good or service?
options: The availability of spare capacity
The number of substitutes for the product
The percentage of income spent on the good
The price of complementary goods

questions.questionText: Explain the factors that determine a firm’s demand for labour.

In Figure 3, the curve XX shows the initial production possibility boundary (PPB) for a toy manufacturer producing trains and buses. Which one of the following combinations is most likely to explain why the firm’s PPB has shifted from XX to YY?
Assess the view that a national minimum wage, such as the UK’s National Living Wage, contributes to an improvement in economic welfare.
Which one of the following is the best example of a situation where there is asymmetric information?
options: A firm operating in perfect competition
A seller knowing more than a buyer
Two buyers being equally informed
Two firms working together on a new product

questions.questionText: Table 2 shows the weekly demand for two products, apples and pears, before and after a change in the price of pears. What is the cross elasticity of demand for apples following the change in the price of pears?

Developed economies, such as the UK, are characterised by high levels of specialisation which involve workers concentrating on a specific task or occupation. This specialisation is possible because in such economies
options: an effective medium of exchange exists.
markets tend to have high levels of concentration.
production is concentrated in the service sector.
production tends to involve mainly unskilled labour.

questions.questionText: Figure 4, shows the original demand (D1) and supply (S) in the market for jewellery. D2 shows the demand after an increase in incomes. After the increase in incomes, the market price of jewellery will rise due to
options: excess demand at price P1.
excess supply at price P1.
increased average cost of producing jewellery.
increased competition between sellers.

questions.questionText: Following a period of unusually cold weather, growers find that many of their tomato plants have been destroyed, reducing the supply of tomatoes. As a result of this
options: the price of tomatoes falls due to the signalling function of prices.
the price of tomatoes rises due to the rationing function of prices.
the quantity of tomatoes demanded rises due to the incentive function of prices.
the supply of tomatoes will fall further due to the signalling function of prices.

questions.questionText: Table 3 shows indices for the total revenue and total cost for a firm in the years 2021 to 2023, with 2022 set as the base year. In 2021, the firm’s total revenue was £180 000 and its total cost was £160 000. What was the firm’s total profit in 2023?
Which one of the following is an example of government failure due to unintended consequences?
options: A government target to increase police officers is missed due to a low number of applicants
Government provision of a free flu vaccine for the over 60s has a low take-up
The government cancels a plan for a new railway line after an expensive planning enquiry
The government introduces a charge at a waste disposal site which leads to illegal dumping

questions.questionText: In an economy, the number of people in work is unchanged but the rate of growth of labour productivity slows from 2.3% to 0.4%. It can be concluded that there will be an increase in
options: cyclical unemployment.
national income.
raw material prices.
the negative output gap.

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows a production possibility curve for an economy producing consumer and capital goods. The movement from point X to point Y is most likely to have been caused by
options: a fall in the exchange rate.
a fall in the trade surplus.
a rise in the foreign currency price of exports.
a rise in the volume of imports.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best describes mandated choice?
options: A limited range of options is provided
Individuals are required by law to choose an option
Options are framed to influence the outcome of decisions
The option is selected automatically if an alternative is not chosen

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows a production possibility diagram for an economy where goods and services are produced in the private and public sectors. The economy is currently producing at point Y. Following a change in government, it is decided that the output of public sector goods and services should be increased by VW. What is the opportunity cost, in terms of private sector output, of this reallocation of resources?
options: OS
OT
ST
YZ

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best describes how a social scientist would develop an economic theory?
options: Apply logic to make connections between normative and positive economic concepts
Create a hypothesis and test whether it can predict the behaviour of economic agents
Develop a number of policies and test whether they are successful in the real world
Form a set of value judgements and test whether they are supported by statistical data

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to indicate that a government is trying to cause a significant change in the pattern of economic activity?
options: A reduction in the rate of tax on income from retirement pensions
A reduction in the tax on a good with positive consumption externalities
An increase in the rate of an inheritance tax
An increase in the tax on a good with very inelastic demand

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the amount of capital, land and labour employed and the output of a firm before and after it expands to increase its productive capacity. Which one of the following do the data in Table 1 show has resulted from the expansion?
options: Diseconomies of scale
Falling labour productivity
Increasing marginal returns
Increasing returns to scale

questions.questionText: An entrepreneur, and sole owner, has £300 000 invested in a firm. The same investment would generate an annual rate of return of 35% if it was transferred to a different market. Table 2 shows the firm’s annual total costs of production, not including the opportunity cost of the capital the entrepreneur has invested, and annual total revenue in the current market. How much abnormal profit is the business making each year in its current market?

Land is an example of a resource that is in composite demand. Land can be used to produce soya beans and for forestry. Between January 2019 and January 2024, the market price of soya beans increased by almost 40%. This was largely driven by the rise in demand for soya beans. Which one of the following diagrams, A, B, C or D, shows the most likely effect of the increase in demand for soya beans on the market for land that is used for forestry?
Figure 3 below shows the supply curve (S) for cakes. Which one of the following can be concluded from Figure 3? The supply of cakes
options: is less price inelastic when price increases from £8 to £10 than when it increases from £10 to £15.
is more price inelastic when price increases from £8 to £10 than when it increases from £10 to £15.
is price elastic when the price increases from £8 to £10 and when it increases from £10 to £15.
is unitary price elastic when price increases from £8 to £10 and when it increases from £10 to £15.

questions.questionText: Figure 4 shows a market for houses to rent. The current average monthly rent in the market is R1. Why is this market in disequilibrium at an average monthly rent of R1?
options: Market forces are likely to encourage landlords to reduce the rent they charge
Market forces are likely to lead to an increase in the average rent and fewer houses available for tenants
Some landlords who would like to rent houses out at R1 cannot find tenants
Some potential tenants who would like to rent a house at R1 cannot find a house to rent

questions.questionText: A large company experiences a significant fall in its year-end profits. Reports suggest it is a consequence of the divorce of ownership from control within the company. Which one of the following is most likely to explain why the divorce of ownership from control may have harmed the firm’s performance?
options: As part of their earnings, managers receive profit-related pay and share options
Due to the satisficing principle, managers act in the interests of shareholders
Moral hazard means shareholders take more risks to achieve greater rewards
Profit maximisation is not the most important objective for all managers

questions.questionText: Figure 5 shows the average cost (AC), marginal cost (MC), average revenue (AR) and marginal revenue (MR) curves for a firm in a perfectly competitive market. The entry of new firms shifts the AR and MR curves from AR1 = MR1 to AR2 = MR2. All other things being equal, which one of the following combinations of statements would be correct for a profit-maximising firm?

Figure 6 shows the average revenue (AR), marginal revenue (MR) and marginal cost (MC) curves of a train-operating firm for peak-time and off-peak passengers. It also shows the price (P1) that all passengers currently pay. The train-operating firm introduces price discrimination to maximise profits. What is the effect on consumer surplus?
options: Falls for both off-peak and peak-time passengers
Falls for off-peak passengers and rises for peak-time passengers
Falls for peak-time passengers and rises for off-peak passengers
Rises for both off-peak and peak-time passengers

questions.questionText: Table 6 shows the size of the UK labour force and the percentage of the labour force belonging to a trade union in 2012 and 2022. According to the data in Table 6, what is the percentage fall, to one decimal place, in the number of workers belonging to a trade union between 2012 and 2022?
